benchmarks.label: Brent

peak.note: Futures intraday wartime high (Wikipedia chronology). Physical Dated Brent (EIA spot via FRED) peaked at $138.21 on 2026-04-07 and was $114.89 on 2026-09-22.

benchmarks.note: Rebounded to about $101.9 on 7 Oct (Trading Economics $102.10, Investing.com $101.84) after three days of declines, as fresh Hormuz tanker attacks and tracking data showing Iran's exports near a standstill outweighed the East-West pipeline ramp-up and the Red Sea advance. Week-ago reuses 6 Oct (1 day prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week.

benchmarks.label: TTF gas
benchmarks.note: Up slightly to €76.62 on 7 Oct (Trading Economics), extending its two-week high on continued risk to Hormuz LNG flows and Qatar's LNG-carrier positioning amid uncertainty over whether loaded ships will transit the strait. Week-ago uses 6 Oct (1 day prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week. Pre-crisis €32.00 is derived from RTÉ's figure of +€14.52 to €46.52 on 2 March.

benchmarks.label: Henry Hub
benchmarks.note: NYMEX front-month climbed to $3.17 on 7 Oct (Trading Economics), a fourth straight session of gains and the highest since 25 Sep, on expectations of cooler weather lifting heating demand. Week-ago uses 6 Oct (1 day prior) — the closest dated figure found this run, not a full week; pre-crisis is the EIA spot price on 27 Feb (FRED). US LNG feedgas and exports are near records, but the US price is largely insulated.

note: Brent and WTI rebounded to about $101.9 and $89.98 on 7 October, snapping three days of declines, as UKMTO logged a fifth/sixth Hormuz tanker incident in three days (12 seafarers injured on the tanker On Peace, 5 Oct) and tracking group UANI reported Iran's oil exports near a standstill under the US blockade, outweighing the East-West pipeline's ramp-up and Yemeni government forces' unconfirmed claim to have retaken Bab el-Mandeb. TTF and Henry Hub both ticked up.
